reasons.R7: The getter/setter plumbing through gc and mathtext is reasonable, but there are no tests, no docs/whatsnew/stub updates, and it adds redundant local imports, a line over the length limit and trailing whitespace, so it needs changes.

Seeding the artists with the current axis limits still feeds data limits through add_patch/add_line, so it is fragile: it still includes 0 if created before plotting and can widen margins. It also has no tests and adds noisy comments and trailing whitespace.
The one-line early return in _find_common is reasonable, but the PR commits three throwaway root-level scripts (one hardcodes /testbed) and adds no real test, so it can't be merged as-is.
Moving the Boolean check ahead of the falsy-self shortcut is the right minimal fix, but a regression test for S(0.0) == S.false is missing.
Adding newline="" to the TextIOWrapper correctly keeps \r in captured output, but the change needs a regression test before merge.
Hardcodes class names and defaults inside the generic _build_repr, leaves dead code (unused parts list), drops the arg sorting so other splitters' reprs change, and adds no tests, so I'd reject it.
Chain serialization is built from heavily duplicated deserialization code with 'test compatibility' special cases, fragile fallbacks, and no tests, so it needs a rewrite rather than a merge.
A clean, minimal refactor that moves the logic onto BoundField as the ticket proposes, but it doesn't adjust the test the ticket points to, so it should get a test before merge.

Reject: silently dropping any method outside a hard-coded set breaks method='nearest' and hides invalid methods, a 'method' dimension indexer still isn't selected, and the PR adds stray ad-hoc scripts at the repo root instead of real tests.

Reject: to_python is not called on attribute assignment or create(), so the reported str() mismatch remains; the change also adds inline imports in three fields and leaves throwaway scripts in place of real tests.

The one-line self.multi_class -> multi_class fix is correct but incomplete: with refit=False and no elasticnet penalty, the l1_ratios_[best_indices_l1] indexing on a [None] list likely still fails, and there is no regression test.
Switching the check to `is None` is the right fix, but the new test points at a target.empty_all fixture module the diff never adds (so it would fail) and has trailing whitespace.

Trying str() first is a reasonable approach, but the PR commits a stray debug script (test_inf.py) at the repo root, adds no real tests, and makes the special-value and exponent handling more complicated than needed.
The fix is correct and minimal for get_feature_names (and inverse_transform), but it adds no regression test, which this repo would require before merging.
The lru_cache is still on get_resolver, which is keyed on the raw urlconf argument, so None and ROOT_URLCONF still build separate resolvers and the bug is not fixed.
Catching PolynomialError around gcd in Mod.eval is a sensible, minimal fix for the reported subs failure, but it ships with no regression test.
A classes_ property that returns per-output class lists should make cross_val_predict(method='predict_proba') work, but there is no test for the reported scenario.

Reject: it commits 17 debug/reproduce scripts, adds no tests, and replaces the real fix with a heuristic that probes roots at 0/±1 inside a bare except, while changing the factors return shape to (f, 1) tuples, which likely breaks downstream code.

get_feature_names bypasses _validate_vocabulary and returns sorted(self.vocabulary) for list vocabularies, which doesn't match the enumeration-order indices transform uses; it also has no tests and some drive-by reformatting.

The rewrite returns False whenever the real or imaginary sum is not structurally zero (e.g. Add(x, 1) with x real), which adds the very wrong-answer bug it should remove; it also calls an expensive expand inside the assumption, and has no tests.
The for-else correctly captures trailing named and unnamed groups, but it ships with no regression tests and has somewhat wordy comments.
Putting the auth back into the netloc is the right minimal fix for credentials being dropped from proxy URLs, but no test covers it.
It uses fragile tick-count limits, turns the grid off with no way to defer to the theme, includes an unrelated removal of the use_inf_as_null context, has trailing whitespace, and adds no tests.
The getter/setter and GC plumbing are a reasonable start, but Annotation, mathtext and other paths are not covered, and there are no stub updates, docs or tests, so it needs more work.
Dropping the stacked dim coordinate unconditionally risks removing the remaining-level coordinate for multi-dim variables and changes squeeze semantics, and no regression test is added.

The fix is sound: it applies ignore, ignore-patterns and ignore-paths to both directories and files during recursive discovery, but it adds no regression tests and includes a redundant topdown=True, so it needs a follow-up before merge.

It fixes the reported override case, but using hasattr instead of checking cls.__dict__ means a model inheriting an abstract parent's field keeps the parent's partialmethod, and the test has trailing whitespace and noisy comments, so it needs changes.

The alias lookup runs on already-stringified annotations such as 'Dict[str, Any]', so it never matches and the bug isn't fixed, and the PR also commits stray scratch files (test_autodoc_type_aliases.py, test_data/, test_types.py) at the repo root, so reject.
Reject: the diff deletes pyproject.toml outright, adds no tests, and the hand-rolled splitter mishandles escaped braces, so after an unmatched \{ every later comma is swallowed.

The logic correctly requires change permission on the target model for auto-created M2M inlines, but there are no regression tests and there is a stray extra blank line, so it needs changes before merge.

Reject: it patches the symptom in three layers with mid-module imports and sqlite adapters that never match subclasses, it can corrupt bytes params through force_str, it has no tests, and it leaves the TemplateView kwargs wrapping untouched.
The fix is correct and minimal, but it adds no test and doesn't update any existing test that treats empty/namespace migration dirs as unmigrated, so it needs test work before merging.

dict_learning and dict_learning_online take a new transform_max_iter parameter but ignore it and pass a hardcoded max_iter=1000; there are also no tests, missing docstrings and lines over the PEP8 length limit.
The one-line qop quoting fix is right, but the PR also monkeypatches pytest.raises using exec inside the library's __init__.py, which is unacceptable.
Rather than making the re-applied forward rename a no-op, it rewrites the backward path to recreate an unnamed models.Index with no name, which is likely to break; it also adds no tests.

The per-database TIME_ZONE conversion approach is right for all three backends, but there are no tests, the SQLite helpers have odd quote/'NULL' string handling and inconsistent signatures, and the comments are noisy, so it needs changes.
A correct, minimal guard that respects a user-defined get_FOO_display in the class body, but it adds no regression test.
The predict change does nothing because argmax of normalized log_resp equals argmax of the weighted log prob, so fit_predict is still wrong; the PR also commits debug scripts and adds no test.
Detecting LogTransform by class name and quietly clamping vmin to eps hides the error instead of fixing the cause in image resampling, changes norm behavior, and has no test.

Minimal fix with a regression test, but running strict IDNA encoding on every ASCII host risks rejecting previously accepted hosts (e.g. underscores), whereas a simple leading-dot check would be safer.
Accessing self.model directly raises AttributeError for fields not yet attached to a model, and no tests were added.

Commits stray debug and ad-hoc scripts, infers category count from ticks with a bare except, un-inverts the y-axis by calling invert_yaxis after setting inverted limits, forces the grid off unconditionally, and adds no real tests.

Uses cls inside instance methods and inside classmethods whose first parameter is still named self (next_lex, next_trotterjohnson, unrank_trotterjohnson), which raises NameError, and adds no subclassing tests.

The `self.model < other.model` comparison raises TypeError because model classes cannot be ordered, accessing `.model` fails on fields not yet attached to a model, and there are no tests, so I would reject it.

Minimal change fixes the reported standalone and Shift-+ cases but has no tests and still mis-handles sequences like '-+' or whitespace-separated separators, so it needs tests and a more robust approach.
Grouping same-multiplicity factors is the right idea, but the bare except, in-function import, misleading hasattr Poly check, and absence of tests make it not mergeable as-is.
Only handles extend='both' and leaves extend='min'/'max' still missing the corresponding edge, with no tests added.

The permission logic looks right (it requires change permission on the target model), but the target-model lookup is copy-pasted into three methods, there is trailing whitespace, and no tests were added, so it needs changes.

The shared SparseCodingMixin.transform now reads self.max_iter, which mixes up DictionaryLearning's fit max_iter and would raise AttributeError for MiniBatchDictionaryLearning (which has no max_iter); it also has no tests and doesn't use the transform_ prefix the other parameters follow.

Reject: it commits many stray debug/test scripts (some empty) at the repo root and replaces SimpleLazyObject with a hand-written wrapper class that repeats the warning in every dunder, still isn't a real str, and comes with no proper tests.

ast.Constant(ident.value) turns True/False/None into the truthy strings 'True'/'False'/'None' instead of passing them to the matcher, so an expression like `-k False` would always match; the change is wrong and has no tests.
Adding the 'compress' and 'br' encodings to the existing mapping is minimal and correct, but it comes with no regression test for FileResponse content types.

Commits three stray ad-hoc scripts to the repo root, adds no real test-suite tests or docs, wrongly extends the deprecated positional-args path, adds a redundant deconstruct in CheckConstraint, and has formatting issues.
The hand-rolled regex-aware splitter has no tests and breaks on edge cases like unbalanced literal braces or nested/leading brackets in character classes, so it needs tests and hardening first.
Passing the key as a mapping to sel is the correct minimal fix, but there is no regression test for a dimension named 'method' and the comment is a bit verbose.

The fix hardcodes a test_/_test.py filename check that ignores python_files config, recursively walks the whole directory for every package, shadows the path variable, and has no tests, so it is a fragile workaround rather than a fix for the regression.
Correct one-line fix forwarding permute, but needs a regression test and description before merge.
Minimal fix for the missing edges, but it checks self.extend directly instead of the existing lower/upper-extend helpers, so inverted axes are likely wrong, and it adds no test.
The change only reformats the same raise with a misleading comment, does not fix the masked AttributeError, and adds a stray reproduce.py script.

The patch only changes the 'P' branch, so 'QD' (Q-format) VLA columns still go to the elementwise != path and the reported bug stays unfixed. On top of that it adds a nested helper with noisy try/except fallbacks.

The one-line check_random_state change correctly makes each class's KFold draw from a shared RNG, so shuffling now varies within each class. It ships with no regression test, docstring clarification or changelog entry.
The one-line newline='' fix correctly stops \r translation in FD capture, but it lacks a regression test and changelog entry, so it needs changes before merging.

The change replaces single-string parsing (inside the q-is-None branch) with an unreachable both-strings branch, which breaks Rational('1/2')-style input without fixing the bug, and it adds seven debug scripts to the repo root; reject.
The coord rename with a dim deprecation path is reasonable, but the PR commits an unrelated edit_tool.py helper and has no tests or whats-new entry.
Passing type_aliases to inspect.signature is the right fix, but the diff leaves many DEBUG print statements that would pollute every Sphinx build, and it adds no tests.

Calling str() inside the function the SimpleLazyObject wraps still hands a SimpleLazyObject to the ORM, so the crash isn't fixed; it also turns non-string converter values like int and uuid into strings, and there are no tests.
Adding the 'Q' VLA format plausibly fixes the bug, but there is no regression test and the extra non-numeric array_equal branch is unexplained.

The _coord_matrix change uses wrong diagonal/all-ones logic and its scripts treat the buggy output as 'expected'; it also commits several debug scripts and an unrelated setuptools pin, with no real tests.
Using __qualname__ correctly fixes nested-class serialization and falls back for locals, but there is no test and no description, so tests are needed before merge.

The one-line _set_col_formats() call reuses the existing core mechanism and has a regression test, but the test has redundant local imports, trailing whitespace and a noisy issue-reference docstring that should be cleaned up.

Instead of just switching the check to v._data, it reports on-disk encoding chunks as if they were dask chunks, returns them in the wrong format (ints, not tuples of block sizes), breaks the 'None for non-dask' contract, and adds no tests.

The core change does nothing (both branches call the same setattr), leaves debug print statements in ModelBase, never touches the real cause in Field.contribute_to_class, and adds about ten scratch scripts to the repo root.

It adds KeyTransformIn for SQLite and Oracle but skips MySQL/MariaDB (the reporter's database), pastes JSON values straight into the Oracle SQL string, and has a dead KeyTransform check on the rhs, so it needs changes.
The core fill_value passthrough is correct, but it lacks a docstring and changelog entry, adds no real unit tests, and commits three ad-hoc scripts to the repo root.
Returning a new IndexVariable fixes the in-place mutation, but it still shares the attrs/encoding dicts, and there's no regression test or whats-new entry.
The None-default fix for copy_X in fit is correct and minimal, but it has no regression test and adds a redundant inline comment, so it needs a test before merging.

repr() already puts parentheses around tuples, so changing object_description misses the real cause (signature parsing/unparsing drops the parens), breaks single-element tuples like (1,), and adds no tests.

It hacks the world_keep selection with a fragile slice.start check and pads dropped world coordinates with an arbitrary 1.0 instead of the world values at the sliced pixel, so the fix is wrong and untested.

Calling set_visible on every child wipes out each child's own visibility, so hidden children come back when the axes is made visible again; the right fix is checking get_visible in draw, and there are no tests or description.

The str/bytes conversions are inconsistent across files: in Python 2 they turn native str methods back into unicode, and in Python 3 they leave PreparedRequest.method as bytes. The block is copy-pasted, and there are no tests, so it should be rejected.
It fixes the reported case, but it uses a broad try/except AttributeError around duplicated code that could hide unrelated errors, and it adds no regression test, so it needs changes.
The direction is right, but it has no tests or changelog, a broad except Exception fallback, and an eager computation in __init__, so it needs changes.

It patches around the bug in the form field instead of fixing QuerySet.none(), changes validation semantics (invalid_pk_value instead of invalid_choice, values no longer restricted to the queryset), adds a query per pk, and has no tests, so I'd reject it.
A small, correct fix that drops None-valued session headers, but it adds no tests and introduces trailing-whitespace lines, so it needs a test and a cleanup before merging.

Reject: union() now returns an empty result whenever any operand is empty (wrong semantics), the none() change uses a nonexistent _combine_queries attribute and does nothing, the form validates choices against _default_manager so values outside the field's queryset get accepted, and there are no tests.
Switching _af_new to a classmethod and using cls/self throughout correctly lets subclasses work, but it adds no regression test for subclassing and has a stray blank-line change.

Replacing lru_cache with a module-level dict breaks get_resolver.cache_clear() used by clear_url_caches, the cache_key logic is redundant, and the PR commits debug scripts, empty files and a bogus tests/settings.py with no real tests, so it should be rejected.
Re-adding auth to the netloc is the right fix, but it uses an f-string in a codebase that still supports Python 2.7 and adds no regression test, so it needs changes.
It adds only a throwaway reproduction script and a binary SQLite database, with no fix to the __in key-transform lookup, so it should be rejected.
It only adds a stray reproduce.py script and never fixes replace_named_groups, so the issue is still unresolved.

The change to dmp_sqf_part (taking the gcd over the partial derivatives in every variable) looks right, but it comes with about 20 debug and apply-fix scripts in the repo root and no proper regression test.

The left-associative division grammar plausibly fixes the unit ordering and the parsetab was regenerated, but there are no regression tests and the grammar change needs verifying against existing CDS unit strings.

Making _af_new a classmethod and using cls in __new__ is the right direction, but it's incomplete: Perm(...) and the module-level _af_new used by other methods still return base Permutation instances, and there are no tests.

The table_alias loop only avoids lhs aliases, not the rhs conflicts that cause the bug, and change_aliases rewrites target aliases into made-up names like T5_1 that don't exist in alias_map, which breaks query relabelling without adding any tests.
Targets the alias collision but has no regression test and also renames first-occurrence table-name aliases whenever they appear in rhs, which would change SQL for many combined queries.
A small, idiomatic fix that parses the property type with _parse_annotation, the same way other directives do, and updates the existing tests to expect pending_xref nodes.

Instead of fixing the regression it adds a FieldError so the query still cannot run, makes questionable class-attribute overrides (contains_over_clause, window_compatible), adds no tests, and leaves a stray reproduce_error.py in the repo.

The core change in prepare_body plausibly fixes binary payloads, but the PR adds two ad-hoc root-level scripts with garbled characters in place of real tests in the suite, so it needs cleanup before merge.

The added extremity segments use hardcoded [[0,0],[0,1]] coordinates unrelated to the colorbar's data-space X/Y (and the same point for both ends), so edges are drawn in the wrong place, with no tests and noisy comments.
The one-line _op_priority bump probably fixes x*Poly, but 11.0 is much higher than needed, which risks changing dispatch with Matrix and other types; it adds no tests and a noisy comment.

Always using __spec__.name changes `-m django` into `-m django.__main__` for package entry points, which likely breaks existing expectations; it should keep using parent when the name ends with __main__, and it adds no tests.

Expanding (1+I)**2 to 2*I just sets im=True, so the reported -2*I + (1+I)**2 case still reaches the 'im and not im_or_z -> False' branch; the bug isn't fixed, and there are no tests, trailing whitespace and comments that only narrate the edit.

Reject: the patch hides the bottom and left tick labels on every sibling axis, including the bottom row and left column that should keep them, it does not fix the extra top and right ticks, and it adds no tests.

The left-associative grammar fixes the order of chained divisions, but it drops the leading-division form (e.g. '/s'), which is likely a regression, strips the license header from the generated parsetab, and adds no tests.
The fix is small and follows the suggested prepare_value approach, but it adds no regression test, so it needs one before merge.
The __eq__/__lt__/__hash__ change goes in the right direction, but it bundles an unrelated SQLite introspection hack, has no tests, and makes the hash change once a field is attached to a model.
Fixes both multiplication orders of Dagger and IdentityOperator and adds tests; the only things to clean up are trailing whitespace and the explicit Mul fallback.
Fixes the string-denominator bug, but the second hunk is effectively dead code and there are no regression tests.
Under --runxfail, an imperative pytest.xfail() with no xfail mark would now be reported as xfailed instead of failing, which changes intended behavior; there are also no tests.
Adds header_rows support for RST write and read in a plausible way, but has no tests and uses unneeded defensive getattr checks.

The fix is correct and minimal: urlconf is normalized before the lru_cache lookup. But it adds no regression test, the new import is not in sorted order, and any external get_resolver.cache_clear() callers would break, so it needs a test before merging.

Mapping the identifiers True/False/None to constants avoids the crash but changes -k/-m semantics, since names containing those words no longer match. It also uses the deprecated ast.NameConstant and has no tests.

It avoids loading data only for variables that have encoding['chunks'], by duplicating the whole loop body, behind a misleading comment. The general fix would check v._data instead of v.data, and there are no tests.
Avoiding rhs aliases looks like a sound fix for the change_map collision, but there is no regression test, which Django requires for a bug fix.

Using str(object) is fragile because IntEnum/StrEnum (Python 3.11+) and custom __str__ return the value rather than 'MyEnum.ValueA', and there are no tests, so it needs an explicit ClassName.member format plus tests.
The added check is always true for imaginary terms, so it silently disables the 'im and not im_or_z' branch in a confusing way instead of fixing that logic directly, and no regression test is added.

There is no description and no tests, it bundles an unrelated pandas inf-handling refactor, and it unconditionally disables the grid with a function-local import, ignoring the theme-deferral concerns raised in the issue.
Using real world values for dropped dimensions fixes the coupled-PC bug, but it adds no regression test, leaves trailing whitespace, and ignores slice start offsets for the kept dimensions.
Converting timedelta64 to float in ns correctly fixes polyval, but it leaves an unused import and an over-long import line and adds no regression test.
Checking __unittest_skip__ on the TestCase instance only catches class-level skips, not the method-level @unittest.skip from the issue, so the reported bug is not fixed and there is no test.
Re-evaluating xfail marks in makereport is a minimal fix that plausibly works for dynamically added markers, but it adds no regression test and no changelog entry, so it needs changes before merge.

The feature is wired through all constraints, but it has no tests, docs or release notes, many lines go over black's line length, and it applies the code to the unique_error_message path, where it is silently ignored.
The trailing named-group fix works but leaves the same bug in replace_unnamed_groups, adds no regression test, and includes trailing whitespace and a noisy comment.
The one-line permute forwarding fix is correct, but the PR ships an unrelated edit_file.py helper script and adds no regression test, so it needs changes.

The __init__ logic overwrites custom messages with the default when no code is given, CheckConstraint hardcodes a non-translated message, deconstruct duplicates kwargs, get_violation_error is unused dead code, a reproduce.py is added, and there are no tests or docs, so it should be rejected.

The new branches bypass the ShapeError check and allow joining matrices with mismatched dimensions, they don't address the all-zero-rows hstack path from the issue, and the PR adds a large debug reproduce script with no real tests, so it should be rejected.
The __str__ override returning str(self.value) is the right minimal fix, but it lacks tests for the changed behavior, so it needs changes before merging.
The fix to sparse row_join/col_join for null matrices is focused and looks correct, but it adds no regression tests for the hstack/vstack shape behavior.
Renaming the dim keyword to coord with no deprecation cycle breaks existing callers that use dim=, and there are no tests or changelog entry.
Permuting the class order doesn't shuffle samples within each stratum, so the reported bug remains; there are also no tests and the change adds trailing whitespace.
Expanding before sqf_list is a heavy workaround that can be slow on large expressions and skips the existing symbolic path instead of fixing the merge logic, with an inline import and no tests.
Adds three stray debug scripts with hardcoded /testbed paths and no real tests, and uses get_prep_value instead of the form field's prepare_value that the issue asked for to handle InvalidJSONInput.
Minimal and correct fix that clamps a zero vmin to eps for LogNorm, though it has no description and relies only on the existing failing test.

It does make shuffle operate within each class, but it ships with no tests or changelog and the contiguous per-class assignment always puts remainder samples in the first folds, producing unbalanced fold sizes.
It does not address the Python 3.8.12 URL-parsing root cause, changes proxy auth semantics speculatively, and adds an unrelated docs theme rewrite plus a root-level repro script with no tests.
Re-implements the existing to_stacked_array with a large, buggy hand-rolled version and adds convoluted squeeze logic instead of the simple drop-on-select fix, with no tests.

The __str__ change addresses the issue, but the extra __eq__ overrides (without __hash__) make the enum members unhashable, and int(other) raises on non-numeric strings, which would break callers; there are no tests either.
A correct one-line fix that passes the key as indexers= so dimension names can't clash with sel kwargs; it just needs a regression test.
A minimal, correct guard that only pops a cwd-like first sys.path entry, as the issue asks, but it lacks a regression test.
A hacky special-case built on string concatenation that breaks inputs like Rational('1/2','3'), and it commits a stray root-level script with a hard-coded /testbed path instead of real tests.
The getter/setter and gc plumbing for Agg/Cairo look right, but there are no tests, no Annotation/mathtext handling and no docs or what's-new entry, so it needs changes before merge.

Keeping the original order in LogLocator.nonsingular fixes the inversion and comes with a relevant regression test, but the added whitespace-only lines will fail lint and the early-return paths don't restore the order, so it needs a cleanup pass.
The fix works by validating the provided vocabulary inside _check_vocabulary, but it ships without a regression test and puts the logic in a shared checker instead of get_feature_names.
Reject: a directory-listing heuristic papers over the regression rather than dropping the __init__.py pattern, it leaves commented debug code, and it adds non-test scripts at the repo root.
Correctly switches to the resolved multi_class and handles a None l1_ratio, but it has no regression test for refit=False and leaves a trailing-whitespace line.
Accesses self.model on fields that may not be attached to a model (AttributeError), orders by model name only, adds no real tests, and commits numerous scratch/empty files.

Hacky special-casing and parent-pointer AST rewriting turn identifiers named True/False/None into constants, which changes -k/-m matching semantics. The code is duplicated, fragile and has no tests, so I'd reject it.

Reject: it hides the error with a str()-based check for 'sinh'/'cosh'/'tanh' in polytools, returns an incorrect False for is_real, breaks the docstring and adds a stray reproduce script with no tests.
Reject: the new Q-format branch indexes column-element arrays by column name (arra[idx][col.name]), which would fail, the np.record branch is dead code, and there are no tests.

Reject: the over-engineered rewrite of _format_float switches to a lowercase 'e' exponent, can exceed 20 characters, adds a new inf/nan ValueError, leaves the old exponent-normalization code under the wrong branch, and commits stray scripts instead of real tests.
The copy_X=None fallback to self.copy_X is correct, minimal and documented as the issue proposes, but it needs a regression test before merge.
Returning the set argument is a small fix that follows existing patterns, the updated test covers it, and it removes the as_relational crash in Piecewise.
Using the process_field_xref hook to pass the current module and class context looks like the right fix, but no regression test covers the ambiguous :type:/:rtype: lookup.

Treating every rhs key transform as an object key, not just the final one, breaks nested has_key lookups through array indices such as KeyTransform('f', KeyTransform('1','d')), and the tests leave unused variables and trailing whitespace.

The object_description enum change fixes the issue, but the unrelated stringify change drops the module qualifier from enum annotations (a regression against the expected 'ugly_enum.MyEnum'), and there are no tests.
Adding a classname-only lookup plus comments does not touch why :type:/:rtype: xrefs lack module context, so the ambiguous-lookup bug stays unfixed, and there are no tests.
The one-line _op_priority change plausibly fixes the issue, but the PR commits three unrelated scratch scripts and adds no real tests to the sympy suite.
The setting_changed receiver works, but it is placed in the storage module rather than following Django's test-signal conventions (or simply computing tags lazily), and it ships no regression test.
The inline (?i) flag fixes lowercase commands, but it also lets lowercase 'no' match as data, which later fails to convert to float, and there are no tests or changelog, so it needs changes.
Falling back to the constructor's copy_X fixes the silent override with a small change, but it has no regression test and adds trailing whitespace, so it needs a test before merging.

Reject: it commits several scratch scripts and a stray test.py, adds no real tests, and the `if value:` change likely stops the preprocessed --verbose (called with None) from ever enabling verbose mode.

Single-key cases are fixed, but `Shift-+` is no longer split at all and whitespace-separated sequences like `M-x  M-s` stop being split (a regression); there are no tests and the diff has trailing whitespace and noisy comments.
Reading level tags on each access is a correct, minimal fix for stale tags under override_settings, but it ships without a regression test.
Adding -v to the preprocessed options and setting nargs=0 correctly makes -v work like --verbose, but no tests were added.
The new code returns (vmax, vmin) whenever vmin <= vmax, which flips every normally ordered log axis, so it is a serious regression and does not fix the root cause.
It fixes the reported BytesWarning, but it special-cases bytes instead of using saferepr for every value, its comment contradicts the code, and it adds no regression test or changelog entry.

It misreads the issue: it fully factors the square-free parts, which defeats the purpose of sqf, instead of grouping factors by multiplicity; it also reverses the coefficient order, swallows all exceptions, adds no tests, and commits stray debug scripts.
The diff adds only scratch reproduction projects, settings files and a hardcoded secret key, and never touches Django's serializer/deconstruct logic, so the bug isn't fixed at all.
Resolving ROOT_URLCONF before the cached call is the right fix and the cache_clear aliasing keeps callers working, but it has no regression test and breaks PEP 8 blank-line spacing (flake8 E302).
The diff only adds an unrelated phpmyadmin git submodule and does nothing about the case-sensitive glossary duplicate-term check.

AutoField normally has no default, so the new condition is effectively never true; this removes the parent-key nullification even for UUID primary keys (likely bringing back the bug it was added for), adds an unrelated helpers.py tweak, and has no tests.

The fix is clean and matches the approach proposed in the ticket, but it changes deconstruct output without updating the existing Q deconstruct tests or adding a regression test for non-subscriptable children.

Clearing the list in place does fix the decoupling, but the PR also changes the shared reset() semantics (which report_handler uses too), and the new test file is full of debug prints and inspect.getsource calls, so it needs cleanup before merge.
Putting parentheses around every unparsed tuple fixes default values but also breaks subscript rendering (e.g. Dict[(str, int)]), and the PR neither adds tests nor updates the existing unparse tests.

Requiring parent-model add or change permission closes the view-only hole, but the same block is copy-pasted three times, a comment is now stale, and there are no tests for this security-sensitive permission change.

It forces input dtypes onto every transformer's output with no opt-in, even for transformers that change values, silently swallows all exceptions, duplicates the logic, adds trailing whitespace and has no tests, so it should be rejected.
Moving the final E-step after _set_parameters(best_params) is the correct minimal fix, but there is no regression test with n_init>1, so it needs one before merging.

The code is consistent and threads violation_error_code through deconstruct, __eq__, __repr__ and validate, but it has no tests, docs or release notes, and the updated deprecation comment probably goes over the line-length limit.
The core fill_value plumbing works, but it has no docstring or changelog entry, adds no real tests, and commits several throwaway verification scripts at the repo root.

It only normalizes path separators in expand_modules and never touches recursive file discovery, so ignore-paths would likely still be ignored with --recursive=y; it also has no tests and an over-long line.
It changes annotation stringification instead of how default values are rendered, so the ugly enum default is not fixed; the `_members_` check is dead, the comments are noisy, and there are no tests.

It probably works only by side effect, capturing the already-replaced no-op tearDown in addSkip; the comment is misleading, it can also suppress tearDown for skipTest calls inside the test body under --pdb, and there is no regression test.

The early return when the index already has the target name addresses the crash, but it repeats the constraint query, adds a speculative try/except fallback, and commits three ad-hoc scripts instead of a proper regression test.

Passing type_aliases to inspect.signature in record_typehints is the right fix, but the change also rewrites modify_field_list so that user-written :type:/:rtype: fields get silently overwritten, which is an unrelated and risky behavior change; it also adds no tests and leaves trailing whitespace.

The guarded pop of sys.path[0] only when it is '', '.' or cwd correctly fixes the runpy case with a minimal change, but it needs a regression test (and ideally a changelog entry) and has whitespace-only blank lines before merging.
Correct, small fix that quotes qop per RFC 2617, but it adds a case-insensitive qop parsing change nobody asked for and has no tests.

The one-line change from UnicodeError to InvalidURL is correct, but the PR adds about ten stray debug and repro scripts at the repo root (with SIGALRM hacks) and no real unit test, so it needs cleanup before merge.

The `'.' in module` check matches nearly every dotted module path (e.g. myapp.models), so it drops the needed imports and generates broken migrations without fixing the real __qualname__ cause; a stray script is also added and there are no tests.
It does surface the real AttributeError, but by calling the descriptor getter a second time (risking side effects), with a no-op try/except-raise and no regression test.

Reordering is now an identity mapping over full_syms, so results come back in the default variable order instead of the requested syms order; this only looks fixed for the symmetric example, and the PR adds many stray scripts and no real tests.

Adding __set__/__delete__ turns DeferredAttribute into a data descriptor, a broad change to a hot path with possible side effects. It is not the idiomatic fix (giving Choices a __str__), it adds an unrelated file mode change, and it has no tests, so I'd reject it.

It calls json.dumps directly, against the issue's suggestion to use the form field's prepare_value. That ignores the field's custom encoder and the InvalidJSONInput case, uses a function-level import, and has no tests, so it needs changes.

Removing the __file__ check is right, but the unrequested change that marks apps with empty migrations packages as unmigrated changes behavior, and the new test depends on a test_migrations_namespace fixture the diff never adds.

Instead of fixing builtin_str in sessions.py, it strips 'B' prefixes and quotes from method strings, rejects any method outside a hard-coded whitelist, and raises for unicode methods on Python 2, with no tests, so it should be rejected.

The core `__all__ is None` vs empty-list fix is right, but the PR also commits scratch repro files (root example.py/index.rst, test/source/*, test_autodoc.py with a hardcoded /testbed path) and adds no real test.

It goes the wrong way: it makes Float/Boolean zero comparisons return True instead of consistently False, adds a broken Boolean.__eq__ (`self is True` can never hold for SymPy objects), and commits about a dozen debug scripts.

Reject: it commits four throwaway scripts to the repo root, and the shared SparseCodingMixin now reads self.max_iter, which breaks or misuses max_iter for DictionaryLearning and MiniBatchDictionaryLearning; no real tests.
Removing the special case is the right fix, but no tests were added and the existing deconstruct tests that expect kwargs for single-child Q objects aren't updated, so they would fail.

_coord_matrix never receives nested CompoundModels (_separable already recurses into them), so the real bug in _cstack, which sets the nested right block to 1, is untouched; the added branch would also return a matrix of the wrong shape, and there are no tests.

Blindly prefixing the current module onto unqualified names breaks builtins like int/None and changes the displayed text instead of passing py:module/py:class context for refspecific lookup, and it has no tests.

The one-line to_native_string fix in prepare_method is reasonable, but the PR adds seven ad-hoc debug scripts at the repo root that hit the network, and it adds no real test, so it can't be merged as is.
The early return in Axes3D.draw fixes the bug cleanly (the Axis3D guard is extra but harmless), but there is no regression test, so it needs changes before merging.

Adding parentheses to tuples fixes the default-arg rendering, but stripping parens from subscripts by string matching is fragile, and the tests only update one expectation, with no single-element tuple or subscript cases.
The logic correctly tells package __main__ apart from dotted module names and is minimal and idiomatic, but a change to autoreloader behavior needs tests in test_autoreload before it can merge.

The capture.py change is syntactically invalid (unbalanced parens), assigns an attribute despite __slots__=(), and dumps ~14 debug scripts into the repo root with no real tests, so it must be rejected.

Silently changes default behavior with keep_attrs=True contradicting its own docstring, reorders apply_ufunc inputs via a hacky wrapper that can alter output dim order, has noisy comments/trailing whitespace and no tests.
The direction is plausible, but it has no tests, no description, a shouty leftover comment and an unverified regex change, and it may change unescaping for commentary keywords, so it needs changes.

The fix only partly addresses the bug: it leaves commented-out code, runs parsefactories again for every collected item, deletes a required blank line (a PEP 8 violation), and adds no regression test.

Reject: the PR commits more than a dozen debug and reproduction scripts at the repo root, adds no real tests, and makes risky changes to core dtype handling (coord_dtype dict handling and dropping .values in PandasIndexingAdapter).
Compiling the regex with re.IGNORECASE and comparing NO with .upper() is a correct, minimal fix, but it ships with no test for lower-case QDP commands.
It fixes the binary-body regression, but it hardcodes a UTF-8 decode of bytes params in prepare_url, which risks mixing unicode and bytes on Python 2, and it adds no regression test.
Raising EmptyResultSet for an emptied combined query is a minimal, likely correct fix, but there is no regression test and the comment is a bit wordy, so it needs a test before merge.
It fixes only MySQL and skips SQLite and Oracle, adds no real tests, and commits two stray ad-hoc scripts with a hardcoded /testbed path to the repo root.

Commits six stray debug/repro scripts to the repo root, adds an unreachable UniversalSet fallback with noisy comments, and returns the set while ignoring the element expression, so it needs substantial rework.
Core fix (set data.cols and call _set_col_formats) is correct and small, but there are no regression tests and the multicolumn format-copy addition is untested.
The str()-first approach addresses the issue, but it duplicates the exponent-normalization logic verbosely, has trailing whitespace and a drive-by comment rewrite, and adds no tests.

The grammar change correctly makes CDS division left-associative and regenerates the parsetab, but it adds no test for multi-division units and drops support for forms like unit/combined_units with a product, so changes are needed.

The re-sync after reset fixes the reported divergence, but there is no regression test and no changelog entry, and an extra stash key is a roundabout fix where clearing the list in place would be simpler.

It misses the root cause, which is proxy URL auth being lost by URL re-parsing on Python 3.8.12. It also injects proxy auth headers into the chunked request body path, where they can leak to the target server, and it adds no tests.
The timedelta64 branch is right, but silently swapping 1D datetime data for its coordinate values is surprising, inconsistent special-casing, and there are no tests.
The minimal case-insensitive regex and NO-masking fix is correct, but it needs a regression test (and a changelog entry) for lowercase commands before merging.

Passing offset=None to datetime_to_numeric subtracts the array minimum from timedeltas, so non-zero-based timedelta coordinates still give wrong results, and the test only covers a coordinate starting at 0s.
Dropping the leftover stacked coordinate plausibly fixes the single-dim roundtrip, but there is no regression test and sel(..., drop=True) would be the simpler fix.
The regex is unchanged (only a misleading comment was added), so commands are still case-sensitive, and the PR adds stray scratch files at the repo root.
Uses an ad-hoc getattr force_key_as_string flag and json.dumps path hack, drops a comment, and adds no tests for the numeric-key cases on any backend.

It works around the symptom by putting a fresh default back on the parent instance inside _construct_form, after add_fields has nulled it, which is a fragile side effect that generates a new UUID for every form, and it adds no regression test.

Using saferepr is the right idea, but it changes the --setup-show output format (strings now print with quotes), the existing setuponly tests are not updated, and there is no new bytes/-bb regression test.

Each class now gets its own derived seed, so samples are actually shuffled within each class, but there are no regression tests, no changelog note for the changed split results, an unused cls_idx variable, an over-long line and a drive-by comment edit.
Switching to the existing to_native_string helper is a correct one-line fix that handles bytes methods on Python 3, but it ships with no test.

saferepr removes the BytesWarning, but it also changes how string params are printed (now quoted) and sets no maxsize, so existing --setup-show test expectations probably break and no tests were updated or added.
A minimal, RFC-compliant fix that quotes the qop value, held back only by having no test for the header format.
The guarded pop only removes '', '.' or the cwd, which fixes the runpy case cleanly, but there is no regression test and the docstring wording is a bit repetitive.

The KeyTransformIn approach works, but it needs changes before merge: it doesn't handle MariaDB/non-native JSON, it builds Oracle SQL by inlining json.dumps output with no quote escaping, and it adds stray blank lines.
The minimal, backward-compatible fix is correct, but no regression test was added for deconstructing a non-tuple child like Exists.

It special-cases Dagger.__mul__ and broadly short-circuits IdentityOperator multiplication for every QExpr (including states, in both directions), which is risky; it also adds no tests and leaves trailing whitespace and noisy comments.

The Call-based lookup avoids the True/False/None Name crash, but it has no tests, leaves stray blank lines and style drift (single quotes, unused imports), and adds an odd comment, so it needs rework.
Only adds a stray reproduce.py script and never implements fill_value on IterativeImputer.

Switching to v._data would avoid the load, but preferring encoding['chunks'] changes semantics (it reports chunks for non-dask variables, returns stale or int-format chunks after rechunking), and there are no tests.

Special-casing __mul__/__rmul__ on Dagger is a narrow workaround: IdentityOperator*Dagger(A) still goes through Expr.__mul__ before __rmul__ would run, it drops I for any daggered expression, and there are no tests.

Building the handle lines by hand with add_artist avoids axvline's autoscale request and fixes the bug, but it has no regression test and the add_line-to-add_artist change for markers isn't explained.

The approach of converting from the database TIME_ZONE across MySQL, Oracle and SQLite is plausible, but the PR adds no tests or release notes, the SQLite 'app|db' string encoding is hacky, and the description is empty.
Minimal str() coercion fixes the reported Session.request path, but it has no regression test, only covers one entry point, and uses bare str rather than the repo's compat helpers.

Reject: hard-codes a special case for a dimension named 'method', silently drops unknown fill methods (likely wrong results instead of errors), renames a shared internal parameter, and commits five ad-hoc scripts instead of real tests.

Commits numerous debug/test scripts to repo root, and the Variable.chunksizes change neither prevents get_chunksizes from touching v.data (which triggers the load) nor returns correct per-dim chunk tuples, so it should be rejected.

Clean refactor that matches the ticket's proposed design, but it has an out-of-order import, a missing blank line between methods, and no test update for the initial-value discrepancy the ticket mentions.
Fixes the bytes-method bug with a small change, but the silent errors='ignore' fallback is questionable, it skips the existing to_native_string-style helpers, and it adds no test.
A minimal, correct early return in Axes3D.draw that fixes the bug idiomatically; it only lacks a regression test.
The regex and unescape changes may fix the issue, but the convoluted word-splitting loop and the unrelated, risky change to CONTINUE verification add regression risk without any tests.

Gating cross-referencing on the autodoc temp_data flag is a fragile hack: the flag is probably cleared before the generated content is parsed, and hand-written py:property directives would never get links; the fix should parse the type annotation unconditionally like PyAttribute does, and there are no tests.

Returning the set fixes the basic univariate case, but it ignores non-symbol first arguments like Contains(x+1, S), repeats a type check that eval already does, leaves trailing whitespace, and adds no tests.

The rename with a deprecated alias is the right direction, but it should make dim keyword-only, raise when both coord and dim are given or neither is, import warnings at module level, and add tests and a whats-new entry.
It commits nine debug and reproduce scripts, and changing Poly.__rmul__ likely won't fix x*Poly(x), because Expr.__mul__ runs first unless Poly gets a higher _op_priority; there are no tests either.

Adding the 'Q' format check is the right fix, but switching to diff_values drops rtol/atol for float VLAs (it becomes an exact != comparison), risks shape-mismatch errors when row lengths differ, has an over-long line, and adds no tests.
Mapping LocationValueError to InvalidURL is a minimal, plausible fix, but it only works if urllib3 wraps the idna error, does not give the expected 'invalid label' message, and has no tests.
Treating min-similarity-lines=0 as off is reasonable, but the PR has no tests and repeats the same guard three times, so it needs changes.
The PR only adds a stray reproduction script at the repo root and does not fix the fit_predict/predict mismatch.

keep_attrs=True copies attrs from `cond` rather than `x`, so the issue's case (`xr.where(da==0, -1, da)`) still loses attributes, the scalar test likely fails, and the docstring wrongly says False is the default.

Widening preprocessing to every single-dash argument adds a complicated short-option parser that silently drops a bare '-' argument, mishandles combined flags, leaves the misleading VERBOSE help text, and has no tests.
The one-line dtype preservation fix looks correct and minimal, but a regression with no test (and a line likely over the style limit) needs a test before merging.
Taking the gcd over every partial derivative fixes the dropped factor, but there is no regression test and one comment is noisy, so it needs changes before merge.
Moving the logic into _eval_as_set fixes the Piecewise failure for Symbol arguments, but there are no tests and a line of trailing whitespace was left in.
The one-line change reuses _parse_annotation the same way other Python-domain directives do and fixes the cross-reference, but it should come with a test.
The None-default fallback to the constructor's copy_X is the right fix and covers both places copy_X is used, but it lacks a test and leaves a redundant comment and trailing whitespace.
Checking skipped_by_mark_key only catches pytest skip marks, not @unittest.skip, so the reported --pdb case is probably still broken, and the change has no test.

Removing the swap fixes the reported inversion, but the later positivity checks now run on unsorted limits (for example, an inverted range whose lower bound is <=0 falls back to (1, 10)), and no regression test was added.
Not overwriting an already-cached reverse relation is a plausible, focused fix across all three descriptors, but there's no test covering the reported prefetch scenario, so it isn't ready to merge.

Setting data.cols and calling _set_col_formats would be enough on its own, but the added str_vals() block overwrites the per-element iterators, which breaks multidimensional columns, leaves dead code and trailing whitespace, and adds no tests.
It re-runs label_outer on every subplot that has a shared sibling, even ones that never hid their labels, it leaves the extra top and right ticks after clear() unfixed, and it adds no tests.
Besides removing the __file__ check, it now marks apps whose migrations package has no migration files as unmigrated, which changes existing behavior; it also adds trailing whitespace and no tests.

Chained exceptions are now serialized and restored correctly, but there are no tests, and reading reportdict['longrepr']['chain'] without a fallback will raise KeyError on reports from older versions that lack the key.
The fix gives the right repr, but it copies __repr__ into both subclasses instead of putting it once on _RepeatedSplits, and it adds no regression test.
Nested try/except Exception: pass blocks and getattr guards hide errors and don't match matplotlib style, and there are no tests for cla()/clf() deparenting.

Re-invoking any class descriptor inside __getattr__ does surface the real error, but it runs the property a second time, could interfere with descriptors that rely on the fallback, adds a noisy comment and trailing whitespace, and has no tests.

Detecting the (0, 0) sentinel and putting handles at the axis limits is a fragile workaround that can misfire on a real zero-width span and may pin later autoscaling, and it ships with no test and trailing whitespace.

The repr fix works, but it is hardcoded in each class instead of using the shared _build_repr mechanism, it adds seven throwaway debug scripts at the repo root, and it has no real unit tests, so it needs substantial changes.

Forcing a subquery when a referenced annotation contains an over clause is the right idea, but folding it into refs_subquery is muddy, the trailing 'or' breaks black style, and there is no regression test.
The one-line fix correctly copies the nested right-hand matrix instead of filling it with ones, but it needs a regression test for nested CompoundModels before merging.

The guard only fires when the to_field value is already None, which a UUIDField default on a new instance usually prevents, so it probably doesn't fix the reported inline-save failure, and it adds no tests.
Passing header_rows through stops the TypeError, but RST.write still hardcodes lines[1] as the separator, so output with several header rows comes out wrong, and there are no tests.

Removing the forced __init__.py pattern correctly reverts the regression and the new tests cover both cases, but the tests have trailing whitespace and the change may break the test that came with the earlier skip-package fix.

Placing the hidden rectangle at the midpoint of the current limits only partly fixes the problem: it is still a data artist that affects autoscaling (for example, before any data is plotted), it reads limits at a fragile moment, and there are no tests.

It adds a new public set_output dtype API with no tests, blindly calls astype with the input dtypes (which can corrupt or fail for transformers that change values), leaves trailing whitespace, and does not update other meta-estimators or global config.

On the y axis it sets inverted limits and then calls invert_yaxis(), so the axis ends up not inverted; it also checks the scale type by class-name string, counts categories from ticks, skips user limits through continue, and has no tests.
The hasattr-based helper fixes the MultiOutputClassifier case, but there are no tests, the docstring has trailing whitespace and lines run past the length limit, so it needs changes.
Dagger.__mul__/__rmul__ return self.args[0], so Dagger(A)*I wrongly evaluates to A instead of Dagger(A); there are no tests and the changes leave trailing whitespace, so reject.

Moving the runxfail check to the end of the elif chain fixes the skip location, but it also turns on the xfail-marker handling under --runxfail, so failing xfail-marked tests would be reported as xfailed; there are no tests, and the correct fix is to make the skip-location block an independent if.

It adds stray reproduce/test scripts at the repo root and no real tests, and it blindly casts outputs to the input dtypes even for transformers whose output values differ; it also skips set_config integration and has trailing-whitespace style drift, so I would reject it.
The two-line fix correctly wires the columns and calls _set_col_formats so the HTML writer respects formats, but it adds no regression test and needs one before merge.
The one-line check correctly turns empty labels into InvalidURL, but it ships with no regression test, so it needs changes before merge.
Casting level values to the adapter's stored dtype fixes the int32-to-int64 promotion in a focused way, but no test locks in the behavior.
Building fresh variables stops swap_dims from mutating the original, but it duplicates the fix in two places, uses private fastpath constructors in dataset.py, and adds no test.
Removing the extra unescape of '' in CONTINUE-card splitting fixes the double-unescape bug, but it comes with no regression test for long null-string values.
It turns a 4.2 regression into an explicit FieldError instead of making aggregation over window annotations work again, and it adds no tests.

Decoding bytes methods works, but the PR commits a stray reproduce_issue.py with a hardcoded /testbed path, corrupts an unrelated comment with mojibake, duplicates the decode logic, and adds no tests.
The fix is wrong: it hardcodes class index 0 and still indexes the 3D ovr coefs_paths with four indices, which breaks true multinomial, and it adds a stray reproduce.py with no tests.
The __array__ dtype fix is on the right track, but forcing dtype in safe_cast_to_index is risky for dtypes pandas Index does not support, there are no tests, and the branching is verbose.

It adds a keep_attrs option but leaves the default dropping attributes, merges cond's attrs with drop_conflicts in a way that is debatable, has no tests or changelog entry, and its long lambda line breaks style.
Making to_native_string return bytes on Python 3 breaks its contract for every caller instead of fixing the body-encoding call site, and there are no tests.
It forces label_outer on any shared axes after cla() even when the user never asked for it, leaves the extra top/right ticks unfixed, has hasattr hacks and trailing whitespace, and adds no tests.
The one-line `is None` check correctly makes an empty __all__ skip all members, but it ships without the regression test the repository would expect.
Commits four ad-hoc debug scripts at the repo root, corrupts an existing comment with mojibake, adds hasattr hacks and unrelated docstring edits, and has no real tests, so reject.
Blindly re-applying label_outer after clear can hide labels for axes the user shared without label_outer, it leaves the extra top/right ticks unfixed, and there are no tests.
The per-artist antialiased plumbing through Text, gc, Agg/Cairo and the mathtext cache looks right, but it ships with no tests and no whatsnew/doc entry, so it needs changes before merge.

Reject: it commits several debug scripts, clamps vmin to a tiny positive value for every Normalize (which breaks negative data), adds a convoluted LogNorm-specific hack that references the nonexistent np.errc, and adds no real test.

Skipping empty keys only hides the symptom: separators in key position still get emitted as plain text (for example 'Shift-+' renders '+' outside any kbd), the regex is unchanged, the 'if sep' check does nothing, and there are no tests.

Clearing the list in place inside reset() means the shared handler wipes the setup-phase list stored in the stash when the call phase starts, which breaks get_records('setup'); the fix belongs in a separate clear() used by caplog.clear(), and it needs a regression test.

Moving the Boolean check before 'if not self' fixes the core bug, but the extra Python-bool special case makes Float(0.0)==False and Float(1.0)==True return True, is outside the scope of the issue, and comes with no tests.
The fix is small and mostly correct, but it has no tests, imports inside the function, calls json.dumps directly instead of prepare_value as the issue suggested, and leaves out ensure_ascii=False.

Dropping empty parts fixes the reported cases, but both elif branches do the same thing so _is_standalone_separator is dead logic, cases like a leading separator still produce wrong output, and there are no tests.

Deleting the runxfail branch outright means xfail handling now runs under --runxfail, which breaks that option's purpose, and the PR adds three throwaway root-level scripts instead of a real regression test.
Always using __spec__.name changes `-m django` and package `-m pkg` invocations into `-m pkg.__main__`, which breaks existing expectations, and the PR adds no tests for the new dotted-module case.
Using a zero timedelta offset for 'm' dtypes is a correct, minimal fix for the polyval regression, but it lacks a regression test with timedelta coordinates.

The fallback calls dmp_factor_list on extension-field coefficients using the base domain, which is a type mismatch, and it skips factoring the lifted factors over the extension, so it is a fragile hack that sidesteps the real norm-factorization bug.
The direction is right, but there are no tests, there is trailing whitespace, and the hasattr guard on _ignore_paths means --ignore-paths may silently not apply during discovery.

It patches the symptom by pointing every stash phase (including setup) at the new call-phase list, so get_records('setup') gets corrupted. The simpler fix is to clear the list in place in handler.reset(), and the PR has no tests and adds defensive hasattr noise.

settings_dict['TIME_ZONE'] defaults to None, so .get(..., 'UTC') yields None and MySQL produces CONVERT_TZ(x, 'None', tz). The SQLite change never passes the database time zone to the conversion functions, and the PR has no tests.
The early return when the found index already has the new name is a reasonable minimal fix, but the diff adds no regression test for re-applying RenameIndex.
The one-line fix is correct and minimal, but it needs a regression test for get_feature_names with a provided vocabulary before merging.

Iterating self._children inside cla() will likely fail on the first clear during __init__, and the PR also adds a stray root-level script, corrupts an unrelated comment with mojibake, and adds no real tests.
The core mapping fix is right, but the stray reproduce_issue.py must be removed, real tests added, and 'application/br' is a questionable MIME type compared with application/x-brotli.
Forcing a refetch for every leaf lookup with a custom queryset is a broad workaround that adds redundant queries and may break existing query-count expectations, and it has no regression test.
The two mapping entries are a correct, minimal fix, but the PR has no regression test for the .Z and .br cases, so it needs a test before merging.

Swapping the check for _is_ignored_file inside expand_modules barely changes how ignore-paths is applied, probably doesn't touch the recursive discovery path where the bug lives, may depend on a helper not shown, and adds no tests.
The diff only changes how typing.Annotated is stringified and never touches cross-referencing of property type annotations, so it does not fix the reported bug and adds no tests.

Putting parentheses around tuples addresses the default-argument rendering, but the PR commits an unrelated edit_file.py helper and has no tests; also, on Python < 3.9 the subscript slice is wrapped in ast.Index, which would likely render annotations like Tuple[(int, int)].

The diff adds fill_value to the signature and constraints but never stores it or passes it to the initial SimpleImputer, so the parameter does nothing; it also commits a stray reproduce.py and has no docs or tests.
Returning bytes unchanged instead of calling to_native_string is a minimal, correct fix for the regression, though it adds no regression test and the nested isinstance check could be simpler.
The Boolean check is roughly the right idea, but Float.__eq__ is now full of leftover debug print statements and the PR adds no tests, so it can't be merged.

The deserialization change checks attributes on what is a dict, so it never takes effect, and serialization is left unchanged; the PR also commits several scratch debug scripts and adds no tests, so it should be rejected.
The hasattr guard in contribute_to_class fixes the override bug, but the diff also includes an unrelated change to database introspection and adds no tests, so it needs changes before merging.
Building new variables instead of mutating dims in place fixes the swap_dims mutation, but the inline import, trailing whitespace, wordy comments and missing regression test need cleanup.
The saferepr fix addresses the BytesWarning, but the PR commits a stray tmp_case/test_bytes.py scratch file instead of a proper regression test in the test suite.
Calling child.remove() while iterating self._children mutates the list mid-iteration (skipping artists), may hit a missing _children on first clear, ignores clf/figure, and has no tests.
The one-line process_field_xref change correctly passes the current module/class context to field xrefs, but it ships with no test covering the ambiguous-lookup case.
The switch to class-aware construction is mostly correct, but it adds no subclassing tests and mixes cls._af_new, self._af_new and self.__class__._af_new inconsistently.
Logic correctly handles trailing groups and the unnamed-group prefix duplication, but there are no tests and the added whitespace-only lines would fail lint.
Only changes the casing in the warning message while still treating MySQL and mysql as duplicates, so the reported issue is not fixed and there are no tests.

The diff breaks cds.py: it pastes formatter code that refers to undefined `pairs`/`cls` into the parser, moves p_division_of_units out of _make_parser, duplicates a method three times, adds a stray root-level script and never fixes the parsing bug.

Treating the final key as an object key fixes numeric keys, but the hand-rolled KeyTransformIsNull rewrites for SQLite and Oracle are risky, and there are no tests for the new behaviour or for array-index isnull.

It commits about a dozen debug and scratch scripts plus a debug comment in core decorators, adds an equal-priority check inside a strictly-greater branch so it can never run, and uses a hasattr hack in __rmul__, so the bug is not properly fixed.

The fix checks the dtype of the underlying pandas Index, which is always object and never 'U' (the '<U*' dtype lives in PandasIndexAdapter), so the restore branch never runs and the regression stays unfixed.

Calling get_level_tags() on every access does fix the stale tags, but there are no tests, the module-level LEVEL_TAGS is left mostly unused, a stray blank line was added, and the setting_changed-signal approach would fit Django's conventions better.

Changing a deliberate no-op backward operation into a rename that relies on the private _create_index_name auto-naming is a riskier change of semantics than making forwards skip an index that already has the target name; it also has a duplicated get_model call and trailing whitespace, and the test never checks that the restored name exists.

The one-line dtype-preserving fix in IndexVariable.copy is plausible, but the PR also adds seven throwaway debug/verification scripts to the repo root and no real tests in the test suite, so it needs changes before it can merge.
Removes the obsolete __file__ check exactly as the ticket describes and updates the existing test to assert namespace migration packages are now treated as migrated.

The patch calls a manager API on what is a single-object descriptor value (likely an AttributeError), does not address the actual deferred-field inheritance cause, adds no real test, and commits a stray reproduce_issue.py script.

Filtering out None session values does fix the reported bug, but there are no tests, `prepare_headers` changes behaviour as a side effect, and the noisy comments and trailing whitespace need tidying first.
Changing elif to if does fix the skip location under --runxfail, but the PR also commits an unrelated edit_file.py helper script and adds no regression test.

The added replace chain is a net no-op compared with the original quote-doubling, so the round-trip bug (which lies in long-string/CONTINUE parsing) is not fixed, and a stray reproduce.py script is committed.

Recursively overwriting every child's visibility is a fragile workaround: it clobbers user-set child visibility, misses artists added later, and has no test, while the idiomatic fix is an early return in Axes3D.draw.

Dropped world dimensions are filled with 0.0 when they should get the world value at the sliced pixel, so coupled WCS results stay wrong; it also adds an unused counter, dead code and a stray reproduce script, and has no tests.

Reject: table_alias now writes to a nonexistent self.change_map and shuffles alias_map/refcount entries in ways that are unsafe, and the diff commits a settings.py inside django/db/models, an app package, a reproduce script and a test file outside the suite.
Returning None instead of False when imaginary terms might cancel is a correct, conservative fix for the reported wrong answer, but there is no regression test.

Commits several debug/repro scripts, removes KeyTransformExact.as_oracle (a regression), builds malformed SQLite SQL with '?' placeholders and lhs duplicated into rhs, ignores MySQL/Oracle, and adds no tests.

Registering terms case-sensitively removes the duplicate warning, but the term role still lowercases its target, so the linear-scan fallback can resolve to the wrong term when only the case differs, and there are no tests.
A small, sensible early return disables the similarity check when min_lines <= 0, but it has no tests and leaves trailing whitespace.

Making _RepeatedSplits inherit from BaseCrossValidator and copying cvargs onto attributes is a hacky way to get a repr that changes the class hierarchy and semantics, when a targeted __repr__ via _build_repr would do, and no tests are added.
The small fix converts a string q to Rational so the q *= p.q string-repetition bug goes away, but it adds no regression test and the comment is a bit noisy.

Reject: it commits five debug scripts, adds odd HAS_PIECEWISE module globals (always False in mod.py, which never imports Piecewise), and makes sinh._eval_is_real wrongly return True for any symbolic imaginary part, with no tests.

Reject: _parse_arglist works on defaults parsed from the signature string, so the isinstance(param.default, enum.Enum) check never fires and the bug stays; it also commits several throwaway test scripts and adds no real tests.
A minimal, correct fix that makes SparseMatrix col_join/row_join handle null matrices like the dense versions, which restores the old hstack/vstack shapes, though it lacks a regression test.
It fixes the common case, but it branches on the raw extend string instead of _extend_lower/_extend_upper, so inverted axes are still wrong, it adds verbose comments, and it has no regression test.

It calls str() on anything with a `_wrapped` attribute in both ContextMixin and TemplateView. That breaks non-string lazy objects, makes the deprecation warning fire every time, duplicates code, adds no tests and never fixes the lazy kwargs wrapper itself.
Re-evaluating xfail marks in the call phase probably fixes the regression, but the bare `except Exception: pass` hides mark-evaluation errors and there are no regression tests.

It commits a stray debug script and adds convoluted, broken tearDown monkey-patching, including cleanup that reads attributes it has just deleted. It never makes runtest skip deferring tearDown for skipped tests, and has no tests.
The one-line `_cstack` fix is correct and comes with a regression test; the only nits are the test's import inside the function and its wordy docstring.

The merge_solution change iterates only over var_t (dropping variables not in the term), leaves redundant dead sorting code, doesn't fix the real permute/syms recursion bug, adds a stray reproduce.py, and has no tests, so it should be rejected.
It swaps one misleading message for a vague heuristic one that still never names the missing attribute (random_attr), when it should re-raise or chain the original error, and it adds no tests.

The ad-hoc brace-counting splitter only covers {m,n} quantifiers: a brace inside a character class can break it, and commas inside parentheses or brackets are not handled. It also commits a stray foo.py and adds no tests, so it needs changes.

It filters discovered files with _is_ignored_file in recursive mode, which is the right direction, but it doesn't skip ignored directory subtrees, it relies on an import the diff doesn't show, and it has no tests for the recursive ignore-paths behavior.

It patches the signature stringifier instead of the description-mode typehint recording, no caller passes type_aliases, the alias-matching comparison can never match the expanded type, it uses a mutable default argument, and it has no tests, so it does not fix the bug.

The new methods are inserted in the middle of BoundField.__init__, so the html_name/html_initial_* assignments become dead code inside _did_change and html_name turns into a setter-less property; _did_change also drops has_changed/show_hidden_initial semantics and there are no tests, which breaks forms.
The added finiteness check on vmin/vmax doesn't fix the real bug: vmin can be finite but non-positive, so log turns it into -inf and the same ValueError still fires, and there's no test.
The new data start_line formula looks off by one compared with the original value of 3, so reading RST tables would probably break; there are no tests and the comments are noisy and speculative.
A minimal one-line `to_native_string` fix at the right spot that matches existing helpers, but it adds no regression test and the diff doesn't show that the helper is imported.

It drops non-serializable chain objects (or a bool) into the report dict, passes an unsupported `chain` kwarg to `ReprExceptionInfo`, never actually serializes the chained tracebacks, and adds stray test scripts at the repo root, so it should be rejected.

The convoluted AutoField/FK condition effectively disables the nullification path (AutoFields rarely have defaults), risks regressions for UUID-pk inlines, and the added models/admin come with no actual test cases.
Catching PolynomialError around gcd in Mod.eval is a reasonable minimal fix for the Piecewise case, but it ships without any regression test.

Only the constructor is changed while RST.write still hardcodes lines[1] as the separator row, so output with extra header rows is wrong and the added test expectations (including an implausible empty dtype row) would not pass.
The merge_setting change is sensible, but the PR monkeypatches pytest.raises with an exec-based shim inside requests/__init__.py, which is unacceptable library code, and adds no tests.
Adds an opt-in keep_attrs but with duplicated apply_ufunc calls, ad-hoc attr picking that ignores variable/coord attrs in Datasets, noisy comments and whitespace, and no tests or changelog entry.

Switching _splitstrip to csv parsing changes behavior for every CSV option (quotes in regexes get mangled), doesn't fix the issue's unquoted example, uses function-local imports, and has only doctests.
Swapping reduce(kls.row_join) for a loop over result.row_join calls the same method on matrices of the same type, so the zero-row join behavior isn't fixed, and there are no tests.
The logic for choosing __spec__.name over parent looks right, but there are no tests and the inline comments are noisy and redundant, so it needs changes.
The tuple-length guard fixes the crash, but the PR commits a stray reproduce_issue.py script with a hardcoded /testbed path and adds no real tests.

Reject: it removes the log-scale limit validation in set_ylim, breaks LogLocator/LogitLocator ordering (it now swaps ascending limits), misindents the set_xlim warning, adds no tests, and commits many debug scripts.

The setting_changed receiver correctly refreshes LEVEL_TAGS, but it has no regression test and registers a test-only signal hook in the storage module rather than with Django's other test signal handlers.
Reject: drop_dims fails on a dimension that squeeze already removed, Dataset() does not take a compat argument, and the PR commits a stray reproduce.py with no tests.
The one-line `is None` check correctly makes an empty __all__ hide all members, but it needs a regression test before merge.
It changes global CaseInsensitiveDict semantics so a missing-key delete is silently swallowed, adds a redundant HeaderDict with a misleading comment, and has no tests.
Moving the final e-step after restoring the best parameters is the correct minimal fix, but it lacks a regression test with n_init>1, which the issue explicitly says is missing.
Ignored directories are not pruned from os.walk, so their subdirectories still get linted (the basename check misses them), lines exceed the formatter limits, and there are no tests.
Grouping factors by multiplicity addresses the issue, but it adds no tests, leaves trailing whitespace, imports inside the function and uses a clumsy multiply loop, so it needs changes.
It renames dim to coord with no deprecation cycle, breaking existing callers, and commits four ad-hoc debug scripts to the repo root instead of real tests, so reject.
Making the combined subqueries empty is a small, plausible fix for none() on union querysets, but it has no regression test.
Correct minimal fix for the refit=False IndexError and l1_ratio handling, but it adds no regression test and has a line over the flake8 limit.
Convoluted fix with an unused sentinel and misleading comments; it only re-evaluates for failing tests (missing dynamic xfail on passing/strict tests) and has no tests.

Storing terms case-sensitively removes the false duplicate warning, but the convoluted for/else resolution scans every object, picks an arbitrary match when terms differ only by case (the role lowercases targets, so MySQL can never be targeted exactly), leaves resolve_any_xref unchanged, and the lookup test never checks that resolution works.
The guarded pop is a minimal, sensible fix for the runpy case, but there is no test, and the PYTHONPATH pop(0) logic that follows still assumes the first entry was removed.

Swapping _DoNothingAction for store_true stops -v from asking for an argument, but verbose mode is still only turned on by the --verbose preprocessing, so -v likely parses and then does nothing; there are also no tests.
The __array__ dtype fix in PandasMultiIndexingAdapter is correct, but the PR commits an unrelated edit_file.py helper script to the repo root and adds no regression test.

Moving the logic onto BoundField is right, but it adds an undocumented public has_changed() method, breaks import grouping and the blank line between methods (PEP 8/isort), leaves a misplaced comment, and adds no tests.

There are no tests, os.path.relpath can raise ValueError on Windows when paths are on different drives, the './' stripping is effectively dead code, and it is unclear the recursive discovery path actually goes through this check, so it is not mergeable.

Skipping the reverse-cache assignment is fragile: it assumes every entry in _prefetch_related_lookups has .prefetch_to, so plain string lookups raise AttributeError, it can add redundant queries, and no regression test is included.
It blindly turns any trailing '\n' into '\r', which corrupts ordinary captured output instead of fixing the newline translation of the capture tmpfile.
The early returns are a small, reasonable way to make min-similarity-lines=0 disable the check, but there are no tests and linesets are still collected for nothing.
Unconditionally casts output columns back to input dtypes (e.g. scaled floats to int), silently swallows errors, adds no opt-in config and no tests, so it should be rejected.
The classes_ property is the right idea but lacks any regression test, has a copy-pasted 'in the chain' docstring and a stray blank line.
Leaves debug print statements in production code, drops basename ignore_list filtering for subfiles (a regression), does not touch the recursive-mode discovery path, and adds no tests.

Only the TypeSerializer qualname change helps (the enum case); the importlib-probing hack in DeconstructableSerializer does not fix the inner Field path, and the test was changed to expect an invalid '<locals>' import path.

Scattered, hacky unicode-dtype special cases across four modules plus a stray reproduce.py script, with no tests, instead of a focused fix that keeps the dtype when copying a PandasIndexAdapter or IndexVariable.

Treating every rhs key transform as a string key breaks numeric array indexes in nested KeyTransform has_key paths (only the final key should change), and it adds no tests and lines too long for black.
The diff only adds two debug reproduction scripts at the repo root with hardcoded /testbed paths and contains no fix to Django's admin inline permission code.

The one-line change is clean, but RFC 2617 only quotes qop in the challenge's qop-options (message-qop in the client response is an unquoted token), and there is no test, so the change needs justification and tests first.
Hacky approach using non-existent item.node attributes and an invalid 'expectedFailure' outcome, duplicated logic, and a stray root-level test file; reject.
Correct, minimal fix mirroring the existing refs_subquery pattern, but it lacks a regression test, which the project requires.
The shallow copy correctly stops swap_dims from mutating the original variable, but there is no regression test.

It adds transform_max_iter but commits stray repro/empty scripts, inserts the parameter positionally (breaking positional callers), reorders unrelated docstrings, uses the wrong versionadded, and adds no tests.
The two-line mapping fix is minimal and correct in spirit, but it has no regression tests and uses 'application/brotli' instead of the more conventional 'application/x-brotli'.

Using str(value) without uppercasing the exponent breaks scientific-notation floats (e.g. 1e-10 becomes the invalid '1e-10.0' because the 'E' check misses lowercase 'e'), and the PR adds a stray root-level script instead of real tests in the astropy suite.
